findings.claim: The strip lets through more than marker and trailer text: a keyword on a trailer line, a prose line starting with totem-close:, and a keyword inside an unterminated marker span that crosses newlines all pass. This falsifies the changeset line 'A keyword line beside a marker is still refused'. The regexes are verbatim from receipt.ts stripIntentMarkers, so this repository's required check also strips these and treats the refs as declared; consumers have no backstop.
findings.counterexample: Write docs/x.md, content 'Totem-Close: mmnto-ai/totem#131 and also closes mmnto-ai/totem#999': pre-change exit 2, head exit 0 (Gemini twin exit 0). Content 'totem-close: is the marker; this fixes mmnto-ai/totem#999': pre 2, head 0. Content '<!-- totem-close: mmnto-ai/totem#131' NL 'Closes mmnto-ai/totem#999' NL '-->': pre 2, head 0. Content '<!-- totem-close: mmnto-ai/totem#131' NL NL 'This PR closes mmnto-ai/totem#999.' NL NL '<!-- end -->': pre 2, head 0. A blockquote '>' inside the span still exits 2.

findings.claim: The new refusal line says 'the auto-close required check and totem pr merge authorize a close by that marker only'. The required check is this repository's .github/workflows/autoclose-guard.yml and is not distributed by totem init; totem pr merge fails closed in consumers without squash-only plus a BLANK squash body. The sentence overclaims in the distributed template (also line 632 and the changeset).
findings.counterexample: git grep autoclose-guard adf39d4e -- packages returns no hits; pr.ts header steps 1 and 4 assert merge-config posture before evaluating.

findings.claim: toContain('totem-close:[^>]*-->') proves the regex text is present, not that the strip runs before the auto-close scan only. The negative control (line 2724) catches a total strip but not the F1 over-strip, and does not assert the refs list excludes the marker ref. Not covered: the Edit shape on the Claude hook, the trailer on the Gemini twin, directive+keyword+marker, CRLF, and a bare ref in a marker refused by the bare-ref rule. No test locks the tracked hook to the rendered template.
findings.counterexample: Reasoned from measured pre-change outputs: every new test except the negative control fails on the pre-change template; the F1 inputs pass all new tests at head while exiting 0.

findings.claim: 'as the receipt's own matcher already does' names the wrong module: the strip is stripIntentMarkers in packages/core/src/autoclose/receipt.ts, not matcher.ts. 'Refreshed by totem init' leaves out totem hook install, which the issue names. Package and patch bump match the issue; no close keyword is next to a digit ref.
findings.counterexample: AUTO_CLOSE_REGEX_SOURCE over the changeset text returns []; receipt.ts:117 defines stripIntentMarkers.

findings.claim: The branch forks at 6a5ca62c, not the stated base 135ea3a9. A diff against 135ea3a9 shows two dependabot pin reverts (lint.yml upload-sarif, spine-spike-linux.yml rust-toolchain) that are main's commits seen in reverse, not branch edits. Bring main forward by merge before pushing.
findings.counterexample: git merge-base 135ea3a9 adf39d4e returns 6a5ca62c; git diff --quiet 6a5ca62c 135ea3a9 on the three edited source paths succeeds (identical).

findings.claim: Does GitHub act on a closing keyword inside an HTML comment, or on the marker text 'totem-close: owner/repo#N' itself? The answer decides whether the unterminated-marker spans in F1 and the newly allowed marker in .changeset/** (an auto-close surface per hook:28-31) are real close vectors. The autoclose tests assume nothing about how GitHub treats comments.
findings.counterexample: Not measured. Write .changeset/a.md with content '<!-- totem-close: mmnto-ai/totem#131 -->': pre-change exit 2, head exit 0.

findings.claim: The issue asked for no behaviour change to either guard; the strip is one. A cure with no behaviour change exists (the marker on the line after its own totem-context directive passes the pre-change hook), so the strip is not the minimal cure. The PR should disclose the behaviour change, the F1 widening, and that this repository's required check has the same widening.
findings.counterexample: Pre-change hook, Write docs/x.md, content '<!-- totem-context: intended close -->' NL 'Closes mmnto-ai/totem#131' NL NL '<!-- totem-context: intended close -->' NL '<!-- totem-close: mmnto-ai/totem#131 -->': exit 0.

verdict: Read 1 of the shield rule-2 change at adf39d4e: blocking=0 material=1 minor=4 question=2 folded=7. Folded by the seat in the next commit: F1 MATERIAL (the strip narrowed to markers whose content is refs only, in both templates and the tracked hook; each measured over-allow shape, a keyword sharing a trailer line, a prose line starting with totem-close:, a keyword inside an unterminated span, is now refused and covered by a test); F2 (the message says 'where it is installed' of the required check); F3 (tests added for the Edit shape, the directive-keyword-marker shape, CRLF, several refs, the bare ref in a marker, the Gemini trailer; the negative control asserts the reported refs exclude the marker's; a parity test locks the tracked hook to the template); F4 (the changeset names stripIntentMarkers in receipt.ts and the hook install refresh path); F5 (main merged in before the push). Answered in the pull request body: F6 (whether GitHub links from a keyword inside an HTML comment is unmeasured; the narrowing removes the span vector from this rule, and a refs-only marker in a changeset is the receipt's existing declared-intent contract, unchanged here); F7 (the strip is disclosed as a behaviour change against the issue's letter; the two-directive cure exists and is why the message names the marker as the channel rather than a second directive).
